title: Your partner's clinic
stem:
You are an F2 doctor in a GP practice. Mrs Ward, 52, has had knee pain for months and would benefit from physiotherapy. She says the NHS wait is too long and asks if you can recommend a good private physiotherapist.

Your partner runs a private physiotherapy clinic in the same town.
instruction: Choose the 3 most appropriate actions to take in this situation.

options.text: Explain the NHS physiotherapy options and how to self-refer.
options.brief: She should know all her options.
options.detailed: Many areas allow self-referral, and waits may be shorter than she thinks.

options.text: Give her neutral information on finding a private physiotherapist.
options.brief: Impartial information lets her choose freely.
options.detailed: Pointing her to the professional register lets her choose without your influence.

options.text: Recommend your partner's clinic, as it is good.
options.detailed: Even if it is good, recommending it without declaring your interest isn't appropriate.

options.text: Recommend your partner's clinic, explaining that it's your partner's.
options.brief: Declaring the interest helps, but you'd still be steering her.
options.detailed: Being open is better, but recommending it still steers her towards a business you benefit from.

options.text: Arrange a discount for her at your partner's clinic.
options.detailed: This could seem kind, but it deepens the conflict of interest.

options.text: Tell her you can't discuss private physiotherapy.

options.brief: Recommending it would be a conflict of interest.
options.detailed: Recommending a business in which you have a personal interest could affect, or appear to affect, your advice.

options.text: Tell her the NHS wait is too long, so private treatment is best.
options.brief: May not be accurate, and steers her to private care.
options.detailed: You may not know the current wait, and this pushes her towards private care.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you give impartial advice when you have a personal financial interest.
explanation.keyDetails: Your partner runs a clinic nearby. She asked for a recommendation. NHS options may be available.
explanation.reasoning: [A] explains NHS options, [B] gives impartial information, and [G] avoids the conflict. The distractors steer her to your partner's clinic ([C], [D], [E]), are unhelpful ([F]), or steer her to private care ([H]).
explanation.competing: [D] is the hard distractor: declaring the interest is better, but recommending the clinic still steers her.

references.title: Identifying and managing conflicts of interest
references.note: Recognising and managing conflicts of interest, including those of family members.
